Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: DDoS attacks and other common forms of how websites get "hacked".

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine a website is like a toy store. Lots of kids (that’s people on the internet) want to come in and look at the toys at the same time.

A **DDoS attack** is like if a bunch of bullies all run to the toy store at the same time and block the door. They don’t want to buy toys—they just want to make it so nobody else can get in. So the real customers can’t get in to look at the toys. That’s a DDoS attack: too many people (or computers) trying to visit a website at once, on purpose, to make it stop working.

Other ways websites get “hacked” are like if a sneaky kid finds a secret back door to the toy store. Maybe the store owner forgot to lock it. The sneaky kid goes in and messes up the toys or steals them. That’s like a hacker finding a way to get into a website and change things or take information that isn’t theirs.

So, DDoS attacks are like a crowd blocking the door, and other hacks are like sneaky people finding secret ways in.
